# Independent review — FA4610-26-R-0031 conveyance study (submission.zip)

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Reviewed as found on disk:
`/filesystem/final_batch4__electrical_task12_conveyance_study__blind/output/submission.zip`
(3 members at the zip root: `conveyance_study.xlsx`, `conveyance_study_report.md`, `route_plan.svg`).
Workbook has all 11 template sheets with the template header row; format checker reports no problems.
Every number below was recomputed by me from the source documents and from the submitted geometry; the
author's scripts/tables were not used as evidence.

## Findings (most serious first)

### 1. BLOCKING — Item C06: OH is permitted and is the lowest-cost type, but it is marked not permitted and CEDB is recommended
- **Requirement.** PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 ¶4.1: "Overhead distribution is not permitted inside the industrial area delineated on C-101 … or within the W-3 dock crane operating area; **outside them overhead lines are permitted**, with underground risers to pad-mounted equipment and buildings." RFP 01 11 00 ¶1.4/1.5: a type is permitted when a route exists on which every segment complies and the type is the predominant (longest) method; the permitted type with the lowest total project cost is the recommendation.
- **What the deliverable has.** `Alternatives` row C06/OH: `admissible = N`, governing clause "PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 4.1 - overhead not permitted in industrial area/crane area"; `Items` row C06 `recommended_type = CEDB`; report §4 C06 recommends CEDB, $462,789 (233.97 $/LF), and report §9 states "all other listed types are excluded by mandatory installation criteria". Register R034 records "OH excluded … C01-C04,C06,C07".
- **What it should be.** The C-101 AREA-CONGESTED polygon is (0,300)-(1150,300)-(1150,880)-(1560,880)-(1560,1300)-(0,1300). Item C06 runs from SS-1 F4 (180,480) south and east along y≈200 to TX-GH1 (1800,122). Measured on the submitted C06 geometry, **1,678 ft of the 1,978 ft route (84.8 %) lies outside the delineated industrial area** (only the 300-ft SS-1 lead-in is inside); it is nowhere in the W-3 crane area (680-1010, 1090-1150). An OH route — 300 ft CEDB riser from F4 to the boundary, ~1,650 ft of 1/0 ACSR pole line at ≤300-ft spans (IEDS 4.9), then an underground riser at the GH-1 pad — therefore exists and OH is the predominant method. The author's own C06/OH take-off (8 poles, 10 crossarms, 2 risers, 6,023 LF conductor) totals **$78,882**, i.e. $383,907 below the CEDB recommendation even before adding the 300-ft CEDB lead-in (≈$70k). C06's recommendation is wrong and the programme total is overstated by roughly $300k–$380k.
- **Evidence.** C-101 Rev 4 polygon coordinates (AREA-CONGESTED layer); submitted `Segments` C06; `Alternatives` C06 OH (direct $55,777.58, total $78,881.83); report §4 C06 table. (C02 and C04 are 16.2 % and 14.2 % outside, so OH is correctly not predominant for them; C01, C03, C07 are 0 % outside.)

### 2. MAJOR — Item C01: ampacity per set overstated (360.38 A vs 331.55 A); the design is within 3.6 % of its ampacity limit, not 11 %
- **Requirement.** PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 ¶4.6: "The soil thermal resistivity at a location is that of the nearest boring … The governing ampacity of a feeder is the lowest along its underground route." TD-15AL-133 ampacity Notes ¶5: "Select the tabulated value for the **next higher** soil thermal resistivity … do not interpolate"; ambient correction applies (25 °C).
- **What the deliverable has.** `Items!G2 = 360.38` A/set (report §2 table "360.4", utilisation 0.888; report §4 C01 "360.4 A"), giving 2 × 360.38 = 720.8 A against the 640 A F1 pickup.
- **What it should be.** The nearest boring to the C01 route between x ≈ 600 ft and x ≈ 670 ft (route vertex 600,715 to about 670,715) is **B-3 at (620,520), ρ = 131 C-cm/W** (distances at (620,715): B-3 195 ft, B-4 282 ft, B-2 203 ft). The next higher tabulated resistivity is **150** (60/90/120/150 table), not 120. Table value 500 kcmil, 2 circuits, LF 100 %, ρ=150 = **345 A**; × earth-ambient 25 °C factor 0.961 = **331.55 A/set**. Total ampacity = 663.1 A ≥ 640 A (passes, margin 3.6 %; utilisation **0.965**, not 0.888). The reported 360.38 corresponds to ρ=120 (nearest boring B-2, 92 C-cm/W), which ignores the B-3 portion of the route.
- **Evidence.** GEO-24-0117 Table 3 (B-3 131, B-2 92); TD-15AL-133 `Ductbank` rows 500/2 circuits/100 % at ρ=120 (375 A) and ρ=150 (345 A) and `Earth_Ambient_Correction` 500/25 °C = 0.961; submitted `Segments` C01 and `Structures` C01. (C02 correctly uses ρ=150; C03/C04/C06/C07 ρ follow their routes: 90/120/120/120.)

### 3. MAJOR — Item C05: the two 36×36×12 pull boxes are not permitted for the 5-in RMC and are not needed
- **Requirement.** UFC 3-550-01 ¶3-11.7: "Pull boxes are used for electric circuits … which require conductors no larger than 1/0 AWG and no more than one 2-inch conduit entrance at each side. **Wherever larger conduits are installed, use handholes or manholes.**" PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 ¶5.3: pull boxes are placed "so that bends between pull points do not exceed 270 degrees". UFGS 26 20 00 ¶3.1.9.2 requires pull boxes at least the NFPA 70 minimum size.
- **What the deliverable has.** `Structures` C05: PB-1 (1200,705) and PB-2 (1400,705), kind PULLBOX; take-off 2 × PBOX (36×36×12 in NEMA 1) plus 12 mh; report §7: "Pull boxes PB-1 and PB-2 are on straight runs so the cable does not bend inside the 36 x 36 x 12 box".
- **What it should be.** The route MSG-A (1132,732) → (1130,705) → (1445,705) → (1445,640) → USS-A1 (1442,642) has exactly three 90° bends (plus the two terminal riser elbows) = **270°, the maximum allowed, so no intermediate pull point is required**. The pull boxes are (i) outside the UFC 3-11.7 size range (5-in RMC, 250 kcmil) and (ii) smaller than the 8 × 5 in = 40 in minimum straight-pull dimension for a 5-in conduit (NEC 314.28, which UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.9.2 invokes). Remove PB-1/PB-2 and the associated PBOX lines (C05 direct cost falls by about $5k; no other item affected).
- **Evidence.** `Segments` C05 polyline (410 ft, 3 × 90°); `Pulls` C05 P01 95 ft / P02 200 ft / P03 115 ft; `Takeoff` C05 RMC PBOX 2 EA, labour 12 mh, $2,584 material; UFC 3-550-01 3-11.7 text; IEDS 5.3.

### 4. MINOR — Item C04: the 5-in HDPE bore leaves a jam ratio of 3.274, only 2.3 % above the prohibited 2.8–3.2 band
- **Requirement.** TD-15AL-133 Rev 3 ¶4.5: "Avoid conduit-to-cable diameter ratios D/d between 2.8 and 3.2; in this range the cables can wedge in bends." ¶4.4: cradled configuration for D/d ≥ 2.8.
- **What the deliverable has.** `Pulls` C04 P03 `jam_ratio = 3.274` (the HDD section, 5-in HDPE SDR 11 ID 4.551 / 250 kcmil OD 1.39 = 3.274); report §4 C04 and §2 "all jam ratios outside 2.8–3.2".
- **What it should be.** 3.274 is outside the band but within 2.3 % of 3.2, i.e. inside the rounding of the cable OD (±5 %, TD-15AL-133 §3) and of the HDPE ID. A 6-in HDPE bore (ID 5.420 → D/d 3.90) removes the risk at small cost; at minimum the 2.3 % margin should be stated rather than presented as a comfortable pass.
- **Evidence.** Supplier quote Q-2608-114 note 6 (HDPE SDR 11 5 in ID 4.551; 6 in ID 5.420); TD-15AL-133 §3 (±5 % OD tolerance) and §4.5; submitted `Pulls` C04 P03.

### 5. MINOR — Item C06: 350 kcmil is not the lowest-cost compliant cable; 250 kcmil also satisfies ampacity and short-circuit
- **Requirement.** RFP ¶1.5: "The recommended conveyance of each item is the permitted type with the lowest total project cost"; PCSFA-IEDS ¶2.2 (ampacity ≥ pickup) and ¶2.4 (0.5 s short-circuit capability ≥ bus fault).
- **What the deliverable has.** `Items` C06: 350 kcmil, 1 set, 386 A/set (report §2: SC 23.3 kA vs 16.5 kA).
- **What it should be.** At C06's governing condition (ρ=120, 1 circuit, LF 75 %, 25 °C) 250 kcmil gives 340 × 0.972 = **330.5 A ≥ 40 A** and 250 kcmil 0.5 s capability **16.6 kA ≥ 16.5 kA** (TD-15AL-133 ¶4.10). 250 kcmil would save roughly 3 × 2,044 ft × ($7.45 − $6.20) × 1.03 × 1.0238 × 1.095 ≈ **$8.6k** in material on C06. (The 0.1 kA / 0.6 % short-circuit margin is thin, which may justify the author's 350 kcmil; the point is that the lowest-cost-compliant rule was not applied/explained.)
- **Evidence.** TD-15AL-133 `Ductbank` 250/1 circuit/75 %/ρ120 = 340 A and `4.10` 250 kcmil 0.5 s = 16.6 kA; PDS Rev D F4 bus 16.5 kA; supplier quote CBL-250 $6.20 vs CBL-350 $7.45.

# Independent review — FA4610-26-R-0031 conveyance study (submission.zip)

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Reviewed as found on disk:
`/filesystem/final_batch4__electrical_task12_conveyance_study__blind/output/submission.zip`
(3 members at the zip root: `conveyance_study.xlsx`, `conveyance_study_report.md`, `route_plan.svg`).
Workbook has all 11 template sheets with the template header row; format checker reports no problems.
Every number below was recomputed by me from the source documents and from the submitted geometry; the
author's scripts/tables were not used as evidence.

## Findings (most serious first)

### 1. BLOCKING — Item C06: OH is permitted and is the lowest-cost type, but it is marked not permitted and CEDB is recommended
- **Requirement.** PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 ¶4.1: "Overhead distribution is not permitted inside the industrial area delineated on C-101 … or within the W-3 dock crane operating area; **outside them overhead lines are permitted**, with underground risers to pad-mounted equipment and buildings." RFP 01 11 00 ¶1.4/1.5: a type is permitted when a route exists on which every segment complies and the type is the predominant (longest) method; the permitted type with the lowest total project cost is the recommendation.
- **What the deliverable has.** `Alternatives` row C06/OH: `admissible = N`, governing clause "PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 4.1 - overhead not permitted in industrial area/crane area"; `Items` row C06 `recommended_type = CEDB`; report §4 C06 recommends CEDB, $462,789 (233.97 $/LF), and report §9 states "all other listed types are excluded by mandatory installation criteria". Register R034 records "OH excluded … C01-C04,C06,C07".
- **What it should be.** The C-101 AREA-CONGESTED polygon is (0,300)-(1150,300)-(1150,880)-(1560,880)-(1560,1300)-(0,1300). Item C06 runs from SS-1 F4 (180,480) south and east along y≈200 to TX-GH1 (1800,122). Measured on the submitted C06 geometry, **1,678 ft of the 1,978 ft route (84.8 %) lies outside the delineated industrial area** (only the 300-ft SS-1 lead-in is inside); it is nowhere in the W-3 crane area (680-1010, 1090-1150). An OH route — 300 ft CEDB riser from F4 to the boundary, ~1,650 ft of 1/0 ACSR pole line at ≤300-ft spans (IEDS 4.9), then an underground riser at the GH-1 pad — therefore exists and OH is the predominant method. The author's own C06/OH take-off (8 poles, 10 crossarms, 2 risers, 6,023 LF conductor) totals **$78,882**, i.e. $383,907 below the CEDB recommendation even before adding the 300-ft CEDB lead-in (≈$70k). C06's recommendation is wrong and the programme total is overstated by roughly $300k–$380k.
- **Evidence.** C-101 Rev 4 polygon coordinates (AREA-CONGESTED layer); submitted `Segments` C06; `Alternatives` C06 OH (direct $55,777.58, total $78,881.83); report §4 C06 table. (C02 and C04 are 16.2 % and 14.2 % outside, so OH is correctly not predominant for them; C01, C03, C07 are 0 % outside.)

### 2. MAJOR — Item C01: ampacity per set overstated (360.38 A vs 331.55 A); the design is within 3.6 % of its ampacity limit, not 11 %
- **Requirement.** PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 ¶4.6: "The soil thermal resistivity at a location is that of the nearest boring … The governing ampacity of a feeder is the lowest along its underground route." TD-15AL-133 ampacity Notes ¶5: "Select the tabulated value for the **next higher** soil thermal resistivity … do not interpolate"; ambient correction applies (25 °C).
- **What the deliverable has.** `Items!G2 = 360.38` A/set (report §2 table "360.4", utilisation 0.888; report §4 C01 "360.4 A"), giving 2 × 360.38 = 720.8 A against the 640 A F1 pickup.
- **What it should be.** The nearest boring to the C01 route between x ≈ 600 ft and x ≈ 670 ft (route vertex 600,715 to about 670,715) is **B-3 at (620,520), ρ = 131 C-cm/W** (distances at (620,715): B-3 195 ft, B-4 282 ft, B-2 203 ft). The next higher tabulated resistivity is **150** (60/90/120/150 table), not 120. Table value 500 kcmil, 2 circuits, LF 100 %, ρ=150 = **345 A**; × earth-ambient 25 °C factor 0.961 = **331.55 A/set**. Total ampacity = 663.1 A ≥ 640 A (passes, margin 3.6 %; utilisation **0.965**, not 0.888). The reported 360.38 corresponds to ρ=120 (nearest boring B-2, 92 C-cm/W), which ignores the B-3 portion of the route.
- **Evidence.** GEO-24-0117 Table 3 (B-3 131, B-2 92); TD-15AL-133 `Ductbank` rows 500/2 circuits/100 % at ρ=120 (375 A) and ρ=150 (345 A) and `Earth_Ambient_Correction` 500/25 °C = 0.961; submitted `Segments` C01 and `Structures` C01. (C02 correctly uses ρ=150; C03/C04/C06/C07 ρ follow their routes: 90/120/120/120.)

### 3. MAJOR — Item C05: the two 36×36×12 pull boxes are undersized for the 5-in RMC and are not needed
- **Requirement.** UFC 3-550-01 ¶3-11.7: "Pull boxes are used for electric circuits … which require conductors no larger than 1/0 AWG and no more than one 2-inch conduit entrance at each side. **Wherever larger conduits are installed, use handholes or manholes.**" PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 ¶5.3: pull boxes are placed "so that bends between pull points do not exceed 270 degrees". UFGS 26 20 00 ¶3.1.9.2 requires pull boxes at least the NFPA 70 minimum size.
- **What the deliverable has.** `Structures` C05: PB-1 (1200,705) and PB-2 (1400,705), kind PULLBOX; take-off 2 × PBOX (36×36×12 in NEMA 1) plus 12 mh; report §7: "Pull boxes PB-1 and PB-2 are on straight runs so the cable does not bend inside the 36 x 36 x 12 box".
- **What it should be.** The route MSG-A (1132,732) → (1130,705) → (1445,705) → (1445,640) → USS-A1 (1442,642) has exactly three 90° bends (plus the two terminal riser elbows) = **270°, the maximum allowed, so no intermediate pull point is required**. The pull boxes are (i) outside the UFC 3-11.7 size range if that clause is applied to the in-building raceway (5-in RMC, 250 kcmil) and (ii) smaller than the 8 × 5 in = 40 in minimum straight-pull dimension for a 5-in conduit (NEC 314.28, which UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.9.2 invokes for pull-box size). Remove PB-1/PB-2 and the associated PBOX lines (C05 direct cost falls by about $5k; no other item affected).
- **Evidence.** `Segments` C05 polyline (410 ft, 3 × 90°); `Pulls` C05 P01 95 ft / P02 200 ft / P03 115 ft; `Takeoff` C05 RMC PBOX 2 EA, labour 12 mh, $2,584 material; UFC 3-550-01 3-11.7 text; IEDS 5.3.

### 4. MINOR — Item C04: the 5-in HDPE bore leaves a jam ratio of 3.274, only 2.3 % above the prohibited 2.8–3.2 band
- **Requirement.** TD-15AL-133 Rev 3 ¶4.5: "Avoid conduit-to-cable diameter ratios D/d between 2.8 and 3.2; in this range the cables can wedge in bends." ¶4.4: cradled configuration for D/d ≥ 2.8.
- **What the deliverable has.** `Pulls` C04 P03 `jam_ratio = 3.274` (the HDD section, 5-in HDPE SDR 11 ID 4.551 / 250 kcmil OD 1.39 = 3.274); report §4 C04 and §2 "all jam ratios outside 2.8–3.2".
- **What it should be.** 3.274 is outside the band but within 2.3 % of 3.2, i.e. inside the rounding of the cable OD (±5 %, TD-15AL-133 §3) and of the HDPE ID. A 6-in HDPE bore (ID 5.420 → D/d 3.90) removes the risk at small cost; at minimum the 2.3 % margin should be stated rather than presented as a comfortable pass.
- **Evidence.** Supplier quote Q-2608-114 note 6 (HDPE SDR 11 5 in ID 4.551; 6 in ID 5.420); TD-15AL-133 §3 (±5 % OD tolerance) and §4.5; submitted `Pulls` C04 P03.

### 5. MINOR — Item C06: 350 kcmil is not the lowest-cost compliant cable; 250 kcmil also satisfies ampacity and short-circuit
- **Requirement.** RFP ¶1.5: "The recommended conveyance of each item is the permitted type with the lowest total project cost"; PCSFA-IEDS ¶2.2 (ampacity ≥ pickup) and ¶2.4 (0.5 s short-circuit capability ≥ bus fault).
- **What the deliverable has.** `Items` C06: 350 kcmil, 1 set, 386 A/set (report §2: SC 23.3 kA vs 16.5 kA).
- **What it should be.** At C06's governing condition (ρ=120, 1 circuit, LF 75 %, 25 °C) 250 kcmil gives 340 × 0.972 = **330.5 A ≥ 40 A** and 250 kcmil 0.5 s capability **16.6 kA ≥ 16.5 kA** (TD-15AL-133 ¶4.10). 250 kcmil would save roughly 3 × 2,044 ft × ($7.45 − $6.20) × 1.03 × 1.0238 × 1.095 ≈ **$8.6k** in material on C06. (The 0.1 kA / 0.6 % short-circuit margin is thin, which may justify the author's 350 kcmil; the point is that the lowest-cost-compliant rule was not applied/explained.)
- **Evidence.** TD-15AL-133 `Ductbank` 250/1 circuit/75 %/ρ120 = 340 A and `4.10` 250 kcmil 0.5 s = 16.6 kA; PDS Rev D F4 bus 16.5 kA; supplier quote CBL-250 $6.20 vs CBL-350 $7.45.

### 6. MINOR — Item C04: segment 3 is classified soil Type B although the nearest boring is B-7 (sand, groundwater at 4 ft) → Type C
- **Requirement.** PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 ¶4.12: classify from the log of the nearest boring, taking the least stable layer within the excavation depth; "granular soils and soils below groundwater are Type C".
- **What the deliverable has.** `Segments` C04 seg 3 (795,960 → 1500,960) `soil_type = B`; Structures C04 MH-1 at (900,960) with `protective_system = box`.
- **What it should be.** For the first ≈135 ft of that segment (x 795–930) the nearest boring is **B-7 (640,1080): SP sand 3–9 ft, groundwater 4.0 ft** (GEO-24-0117 Table 2 classifies B-7 as B, which the author's own finding F06 corrects to C). Trench depth 3.71 ft is inside the sand, so the segment (and MH-1, 8 ft deep) is Type C. No cost effect because the trench is <5 ft and the manhole is shielded, but the register/report statement "B" is wrong for that reach.
- **Evidence.** GEO-24-0117 Table 3 / Appendix A B-7 log and groundwater; submitted `Segments` C04 and `Structures` C04; author's finding F06.

### 7. MINOR — Transformer terminal points: routes end at offset text labels, not at the pad reference points
- **Requirement.** C-101 Rev 4 General Note 9: "PAD-MOUNTED TRANSFORMER PADS ARE SHOWN CENTERED ON THE PAD REFERENCE POINT"; RFP ¶1.3: "Pad-mounted transformers are served at the pad."
- **What the deliverable has.** C04 seg 5 ends at (1760,1152), C06 seg 4 at (1800,122), C07 seg 3 at (1030,1172) — the text-label positions. Author's finding F22 records the 8-ft offset but chooses the labels.
- **What it should be.** The 6 × 6 ft pad squares are centred at **(1760,1160), (1800,130), (1030,1180)**; the label positions are 5 ft outside the pad edge, so the ductbank as drawn stops 5 ft short of the transformer pad. Route lengths are 8 ft short each (≤1.2 % of item length, within the 3 % quantity tolerance), but the terminal geometry should be corrected to the pad centres.
- **Evidence.** C-101 Rev 4 TERMINALS LWPOLYLINEs (pad squares) and TEXT labels; C-101 General Note 9; submitted `Segments` C04/C06/C07.

### 8. MINOR — Report §3 misdescribes the C02 cover: the road crossing is at 30 in, not 63 in
- **Requirement.** RFP ¶"Segments": `cover_in` is finished grade to top of duct; report must present the design consistently with the workbook.
- **What the deliverable has.** Report §3: "C02 is at 30 in cover except 63 in where it passes beneath the T-2 telecom ductbank (15 in vertical separation) **and at its road crossing**."
- **What it should be.** The 63-in reach is C02 seg 2 at x=340 (T-2 crossing, y≈430), about 420 ft from Mission Drive. The Mission Drive crossing is **seg 4 (755,410 → 795,410, JB) at 30 in cover** (`Segments` C02 row 4). The sentence wrongly implies the road crossing is at 63 in.
- **Evidence.** `Segments` C02 rows 2 and 4; report §3.

### 9. MINOR — Gasoline compactor priced with the diesel fuel ratio
- **Requirement.** RFP ¶3.3: equipment rates adjusted for fuel and FOG per EP 1110-1-8 ¶3.9/3.10 using the jobsite fuel prices of the fuel supplier invoice (diesel $4.38, gasoline $5.12).
- **What the deliverable has.** `EquipmentRates` C10BO003 = $2.7942/hr (report §8 $2.79).
- **What it should be.** EP 1110-1-8 Vol 7 lists C10BO003 as **G (gasoline)**: base average $1.95, FUEL $0.81, FOG $0.09, so adjusted = (1.95 − 0.90) + 0.90 × (5.12/2.49 = 2.0562) = **$2.9006/hr**, not $2.7942 (which uses the diesel ratio 4.38/2.26 = 1.9381). Effect on the work is < $50.
- **Evidence.** EP 1110-1-8 Vol 7 p.72 and p.280 (C10BO003, 4 HP, "G", 1.95 / 0.81 / 0.09); Fuel invoice FSI-0826-2207 ($5.12 gasoline, $4.38 diesel); report §2/§8.

## Checks performed that found no error (for the record)
- **Take-off vs geometry.** I rebuilt every recommended item's CE/JB/HDD quantities from the submitted `Segments`/`Structures` polylines with the RFP ¶3.7 conventions (envelope, trench, concrete, rebar, spacers, ground/tape, pavement clipping, TBOX, dewatering, manhole prism, cable circuit-feet, terminations, fireproofing, C05 RMC/elbows/firestop/seismic): **all quantities agree with the `Takeoff` sheet** except PAVE-CUT C03 108.787 vs 108.844 SY (0.05 %). Circuit-feet and conductor-feet agree for all items (e.g. C01 1,828.416 circuit-ft / 5,485.248 conductor-ft).
- **Roll-up.** Direct costs from the `Takeoff` sheet reproduce every `Alternatives` figure, JOOH 9.5 %, HOOH 4.5 %, profit 7.9494 % (weighted guidelines, UFC 3-740-05 11-2.2: size 0.06143, period 0.08478, subcontracting 0.08625), escalation 1.019388 (UFS 3-701-01 Table 4-2 interpolation 2026-09-15 → 2027-08-18), contingency 5 %, SIOH 5.7 %; programme total **$2,132,804.86** matches the report.
- **Bond.** Sum of the seven recommended (direct + JOOH + HOOH + profit) = $1,862,878.43; Sierra Surety Class B graduated premium $21,628.78 × 1.03 (3 months > 12) = $22,277.65 → effective 1.195872 %, exactly the `Markups` value; each alternative's bond follows.
- **Ampacity/short-circuit (other items).** C02 663.1 A ≥ 560 A; C03 466.1 A ≥ 400 A (ρ 90, 56-in reach → 72-in depth factor 0.951); C04 330.5 A ≥ 60 A; C05 320 A ≥ 200 A (40 °C conduit in air); C06 386 A ≥ 40 A; C07 330.5 A ≥ 120 A; 0.5 s short-circuit 33.3/33.3/33.3/16.6/16.6/23.3/16.6 kA ≥ 16.5/16.5/16.5/14.2/15.8/16.5/14.2 kA (minimum margin C05 0.952, as reported).
- **Pulling.** Recomputing C01 P02 by TD-15AL-133 ¶4.7/4.8 (100 lb feed, wc = 1.1676, f = 0.35, W = 4.44 lb/ft, 25-ft field bends) gives 734.5 lb and SWBP 11.1 lb/ft — exactly the submitted values; all `Pulls` tensions are below 0.006 lb/cmil × 2 conductors (C03 2,055 lb vs 6,000 lb max) and all SWBP below the approved 600 lb/ft (max C03 343 lb/ft).
- **C05 space/SCIF.** Route y=705 is 15 ft from the IT-1 south wall (10-ft keep-out), passes only rooms with ≥14 in (RMC needs 6 in), and does not use COR-2 or the SCIF; RMC is the only permitted C05 type (EMT barred by UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.6.7, ladder tray by UFC 3-520-01 Table 3-1 art. 328, enclosed tray by the 14-in COR-1D).
- **Format.** `ahpele_check.py` on `submission.zip` and the workbook: no problems; all 11 sheets, template headers in row 1, live formulas in `Alternatives` K–U, `LaborRates` G and `Items` I–J.

## Summary
One blocking error (C06 OH wrongly excluded, recommendation and programme total wrong), one major ampacity error (C01 360.38 vs 331.55 A/set), one major C05 design item (non-permitted/unnecessary pull boxes), plus six minor items. The take-off, roll-up, bond and pulling arithmetic are otherwise sound.

2.4 Short-circuit withstand. Each set of medium-voltage cable shall withstand the full available fault current of its source bus
for the backup (breaker-failure) clearing time, both as stated in the current protective device settings schedule: the
conductor short-circuit capability tabulated by the cable manufacturer for the tabulated duration equal to or next longer than
the clearing time shall not be less than the available fault current.
4 SITE DISTRIBUTION
4.1 Conveyance selection follows UFC 3-550-01 paragraph 3-11 and this chapter. Overhead distribution is not permitted
inside the industrial area delineated on C-101 (Area Development Plan 2024, a congested industrial area) or within the W-3
dock crane operating area; outside them overhead lines are permitted, with underground risers to pad-mounted equipment
and buildings.
4.2 Primary circuits between underground structures, and between underground structures and equipment, shall be
concrete-encased ductbanks (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1; UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.9). Direct-buried cable and conduit without
concrete encasement are not permitted for the installation's primary distribution.
4.3 Existing pavement. Perimeter Road, Mission Drive and the MB-1 access drive shall not be open-cut; cross them by
directional bore or jack-and-bore (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2). Parking lot P-1 and the CUP-1 service yard may be saw-cut and
patched; ductbanks under them shall be reinforced, and the encasement shall extend at least 5 ft beyond the edges of the
paving (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8.1). Directional bores are used only for the crossings listed in UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1 (roads,
parking lots, bodies of water); a bore shall not extend more than 50 ft beyond the pavement edge or channel bank on either
side. Channel DC-1 shall not be open-cut.
4.4 Redundancy. Conveyances of SS-1 bus A feeders (F1, F3) and bus B feeders (F2, F4) shall not share ductbanks or
underground structures and shall be at least 20 ft apart (centerline to centerline), except within 50 ft of the SS-1 fence or of
the MB-1 walls.

4.10 Underground structures: UFC 3-550-01 3-11.5 and 3-11.6, including the Air Force distances of 3-11.5.5; manholes are

(circuits up to 15 kV).

0002)
Solicitation FA4610-26-R-0031, project PCSFA 24-0117: Pacific Crest Space Force Annex - Mission Support Facility MB-1
and Central Utility Plant CUP-1, 13.8 kV Site Distribution. Issued 2026-08-28.
PART 1 GENERAL
1.1 Schedule. Study date 2026-09-15. Bid opening (sealed bidding) 2026-10-08. Construction start 2027-01-04; duration 15
months; midpoint of construction 2027-08-18.

1.3 Terminals. SS-1 feeders leave the substation at the duct stub-outs shown on C-101. Ductbanks to MB-1 and CUP-1
enter the electrical rooms through the exterior wall within the entry zones shown on C-101, perpendicular to the wall.
Pad-mounted transformers are served at the pad. Item C05 runs inside MB-1 between the MSG-A and USS-A1 connection
points on E-101.
1.4 Conveyance types to be evaluated. Items C01, C02, C03, C04, C06 and C07: CEDB (concrete-encased ductbank),
UEDB (conduit ductbank without encasement), DBC (direct-buried cable), HDD (directional bore as the method of the entire
run), OH (overhead pole line with underground risers). Item C05: RMC (rigid metal conduit), EMT (electrical metallic tubing),
TRAY-EN (fully enclosed solid-bottom covered cable tray), TRAY-LD (ladder cable tray). Each type is evaluated as the
predominant method of the run on the route the contractor would build with it, including the crossing treatments the criteria
require. A type is permitted for an item when a route exists on which every segment complies with the governing criteria and
that type is the predominant (longest) method. The study states for each type whether the governing criteria permit it for the
item and cites the deciding clause, and prices every type, permitted or not.
1.5 The recommended conveyance of each item is the permitted type with the lowest total project cost. It shall be designed
to the 10 percent level: route, methods, depths, duct arrangements, structures, cable, pulling plan and excavation
protection.
1.6 The study report presents, for each item, the recommendation and tables of labor hours, rates used and cost per linear
foot of every type evaluated. Errors found in Government-furnished documents shall be reported with the correction used.
PART 2 LABOR CLASSIFICATION PLAN
2.1 The wage determination is Attachment J-3. Wage determinations and their modifications apply as provided in 29 CFR
1.6. The Contracting Officer designates the classifications that apply to the work (29 CFR 1.6(b)(1)) as follows; crew
compositions are the contractor's crew book.

2.2 The Annex is not a military base listed for premium pay in the wage determination.
PART 3 ESTIMATING BASIS
3.1 Structure. Estimates follow UFC 3-740-05: direct cost (labor, construction equipment, materials, subcontracts), job office
overhead, home office overhead, profit, bond, escalation, design contingency and SIOH. The estimate is a bottom-up
estimate priced with the local wage determination, local quotes and the Region VII equipment schedule; location factors are
applied only as UFS 3-701-01 permits.
3.2 Labor. Labor hours = quantity x labor unit from the contractor's labor-unit database, with the conversions and multipliers
stated in the database. Labor cost = hours x the average loaded rate of the crew. Loaded rate = base rate x (1 + burden
percent) + fringe; burden percent = FICA + FUTA + state unemployment + workers' compensation of the classification's
class code, applied to base wages only.
3.3 Construction equipment. EP 1110-1-8 Region VII total hourly rates, adjusted for fuel and FOG per EP 1110-1-8
paragraphs 3.9 and 3.10 using the jobsite fuel prices of the fuel supplier invoice. Rental equipment at the rental quote. Crew
hours = labor hours / crew size; equipment hours = crew hours x the number of units in the crew.
3.4 Materials. Quoted unit price x (1 + recommended waste allowance) x the quote's price-index adjustment to the latest
index published before the study date x (1 + 9.5 percent sales tax).
3.5 Subcontracts. At the subcontract quotes; no waste, tax or adjustment.
3.6 Roll-up. JOOH 9.5 percent of direct cost. HOOH 4.5 percent of direct cost plus JOOH. Profit by the weighted guidelines
method of UFC 3-740-05 11-2.1 and 11-2.2 applied to direct cost plus JOOH plus HOOH, with the factor rates of the profit
computation sheet below; weights: Degree of Risk 0.08, Relative Difficulty 0.09, Contractor's Investment 0.06, Assistance
by Government 0.07; Size of the Job, Period of Performance and Subcontracting weighted per 11-2.2 for the programmed
amount of $4,200,000, the 15-month performance period and 30 percent subcontracting. Bond: surety rate letter applied to
the sum, over the seven items' recommended designs, of direct cost plus JOOH, HOOH and profit; the resulting effective
rate is applied to every alternative. Escalation (UFC 3-740-05 13-4): a separate element equal to (escalation factor - 1) x
(cost including bond), the escalation factor being the UFS 3-701-01 Table 4-2 factor at the midpoint of construction divided
by the factor at the study date, interpolated linearly by day between the tabulated dates. Design contingency 5.0 percent of
contract cost. SIOH 5.7 percent applied per UFC 3-740-05 13-3.2. Cost per linear foot = total project cost / route length of
the alternative.

3.7 Take-off conventions. Quantities of each alternative are taken off its route as follows (lengths along the route polyline;
units of the cost documents). A ductbank segment occupied by circuits of k items, and a manhole used by k items, is taken
off once and allocated in equal shares of 1/k to each item.
Item
Convention
Trench and ductbank section (CE,
UE)
Duct envelope width = columns x duct OD + 3 in between ducts (+ 3 in concrete each side for CE); height
likewise with rows. Trench bottom width = envelope width + 6 in each side; trench depth = cover + envelope
height + 3 in bedding. Duct OD per the conduit dimensions of the supplier quote.
Direct-buried cable trench (DB)
Width 8 in; triplexed cable height 2.155 x cable OD; depth = cover + cable height + 3 in; sand = trench width
x (cable height + 2 x 3 in).
Excavation (EX-MACH, bank CY)
Trench bottom width x depth per foot; where the depth is 5 ft or more and the protective system is sloping,
average width = bottom width + slope x depth. DB trenches: EX-TRCH per foot.
Backfill (BF-COMP, bank CY)
Excavation - envelope volume (CE, UE) - sand volume (UE, DB); manholes: excavation - manhole outside
volume - rock base.
Sand (SAND-BED, SAND)
UE: trench bottom width x (envelope height + 6 in + 3 in) - envelope; DB as above.
Concrete (CONC-PL, CONC-3000)
CE: (envelope width x height - ducts x pi/4 x OD^2) per foot.
Reinforcement (REBAR, REBAR-4)
Reinforced CE: 4 No. 4 bars (6 where the envelope is wider than 30 in) at 0.668 lb/ft, plus No. 3 ties (0.376
lb/ft) of length 2(w-3 in)+2(h-3 in) at 3 ft centers (floor(L/3)+1 ties).
Ducts (DUCT-CE / DUCT-UE with
EB20-n / SCH40-n)
Ducts x length. Spacers (SPACER): ducts x (floor(L/5)+1).
Ground, tape (GND-DB, GND-4/0,
TAPE, TAPE-DET)
One per ductbank per foot; tape per foot of trench (CE, UE, DB).
Pavement (PAVE-CUT, ASPHALT)
Length in pavement x (trench top width + 2 ft) / 9 (SY).
Dewatering (DEWATER)
Trench length whose depth exceeds the groundwater depth of the governing boring; 25 LF per manhole
below groundwater.
Trench shield (TBOX)
Length of trench 5 ft or deeper protected by shield; 20 LF per shielded manhole excavation.
Manholes (MH-SET, MH-PRECAST,
MH-BASE, ROCK-BASE)
Precast outside plan 7.33 x 9.33 ft, excavation 8 ft deep with 2 ft clearance each side (sloped per protective
system; prismoidal volume), 0.5 ft rock base over the excavation bottom.
Bores and jacked crossings
SUB-HDD per bore (conduits in the bore, length, cover, pits, minimum); SUB-JB / SUB-JS per crossing at
the quotes; RGS conduit for JB and JS from the supplier quote, conduits x length.
MV cable (PULL-MV / PULL-MV-L /
DBC-LAY; CBL-size)
DBC-LAY for the circuit-feet of direct-buried segments and the pulling code for the remainder. Circuit-feet =
sets x (underground route length + 6 ft per manhole + (10 ft termination + 8 ft riser) per equipment terminal
+ 40 ft per riser pole); conductor-feet = 3 x circuit-feet.
Terminations, splices, fireproofing
TERM-MV 3 per set per equipment terminal (riser pole terminations are in RISER); SPLICE-MV 3 per set
per splice, splices where a pull length of cable exceeds the maximum reel length; FIREPROOF 12
conductor-ft per conductor per manhole.
Overhead (POLE-SET, POLE-45/50,
POLE-HOLE, XARM, GUY, RISER,
STRING, ACSR)
One set, hole and crossarm per pole (two crossarms on dead-ends); guys as designed; RISER per circuit
per riser pole; conductor-feet = 3 x overhead length x 1.015.
Building (C05)
RMC/EMT: sets x (route length + 2 rises); elbows sets x (bends + 2); firestop per set per rated wall. Tray:
tray, cover (enclosed), bond per foot; RMC drops sets x 2 rises with 2 elbows per set; sleeves per 2-hour
wall; firestop per set per 1-hour wall. Seismic braces ceil(L/40)+ceil(L/80). Cable circuit-feet = sets x (route
+ 2 rises + 2 x 10 ft); TERM-IN 6 per set.
3.8 Pairing of labor and material codes: duct and conduit codes with the duct/conduit material of their size;
CONC-PL/CONC-3000; REBAR/REBAR-4; GND-DB/GND-4/0; TAPE/TAPE-DET; PAVE-CUT/ASPHALT;
MH-SET/MH-PRECAST; MH-BASE/ROCK-BASE; SAND-BED/SAND; cable pulling/CBL-size; TERM-MV and
TERM-IN/TERM-KIT; SPLICE-MV/SPLICE-KIT; FIREPROOF/FIRETAPE; POLE-SET/POLE-45 or POLE-50;
XARM/XARM-ASSY; GUY/GUY-ASSY; RISER/RISER-ASSY; STRING/ACSR-size; RMC-5/RGS-5; EMT-4/EMT-4IN;
ELBOW-5/ELBOW-RGS5; PBOX/PBOX-36; TRAY-24/TRAY-24-SB or TRAY-24-LD; TRAY-COV/TRAY-COV-24;
TRAY-BOND/BOND-2; FIRE-SLV/FIRE-SLV-4; FIRE-RMC/FIRESTOP-RMC5; SEISMIC/SEISMIC-BR.

            if l<1e-12: continue

1. Introduction
This report presents the results of the geotechnical investigation performed for the new underground and overhead 13.8 kV
site distribution serving the Mission Support Facility MB-1, the Central Utility Plant CUP-1 and outlying loads. The purpose
of the investigation was to characterize the subsurface soils along the anticipated conveyance corridors, provide soil thermal
resistivity data for cable ampacity calculations, and provide information for excavation planning, backfill and pavement
restoration.
2. Site Description and Published Soil Information
The site is a developed, generally level industrial area with buildings, paved roads and parking, an active rail spur and an
open drainage channel along the eastern portion of the site. Finished grades range from approximately elevation 39 to 44 ft.
Coordinates in this report are in site grid feet consistent with drawing C-101.
The site lies within NRCS map unit 2478607, Urban land-Thums-Windfetch complex, 0 to 2 percent slopes (Los Angeles
County, California, Southeastern Part, survey area CA696). The map unit is composed of Urban land (50 percent), Thums
(20 percent) and Windfetch (15 percent) soils with minor components. The Thums and Windfetch components are well
drained to moderately well drained clay loams with argillic subsoil horizons; the published risk of corrosion of uncoated steel
is High. Published map-unit data are generalized and do not replace the site specific boring information.
Source: Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Soil Survey Geographic (SSURGO)
Database, accessed through Soil Data Access. The USDA-NRCS is acknowledged as the data source.
3. Field Exploration Program
Twelve borings (B-1 through B-12) were drilled between 2025-04-07 and 2025-04-10 with a truck-mounted drill rig using 8 in
hollow-stem augers to a depth of 15 ft below existing grade. Standard penetration tests were performed at 2.5 ft intervals to
10 ft and at 5 ft intervals thereafter; relatively undisturbed samples were recovered in cohesive soils. Soils were logged in
the field by a staff geologist and classified in accordance with the Unified Soil Classification System (USCS). Boring
locations were surveyed with RTK GNSS. Boreholes were backfilled with bentonite grout and patched at the surface.
Individual boring logs are presented in Appendix A and in electronic form (files B-01.csv to B-12.csv).

4. Subsurface Conditions
The borings generally encountered stiff lean clay (CL) from the surface to the maximum depth explored. Fill consisting of
lean clay or clayey sand with debris was encountered at B-1 and B-3 to depths of 2 and 6 ft. Granular soils were
encountered at two locations: poorly graded sand (SP) between 3 and 9 ft at B-7, near the CUP-1 yard, and silty sand (SM)
between 2 and 12 ft at B-10, adjacent to the drainage channel. Detailed stratification is shown on the logs; transitions
between strata may be gradual.

unconfined compressive strength. The unconfined compressive strength of cohesive samples was measured with a
calibrated pocket penetrometer on the recovered samples and confirmed by unconfined compression tests on selected
samples. Granular samples were not tested for compressive strength. Results by layer are summarized below.

9. Backfill and Pavement Restoration
On-site lean clay free of debris may be reused as general trench backfill above the select backfill zone, placed in loose lifts
not exceeding 8 in and compacted to at least 90 percent of maximum dry density (95 percent within 2 ft of pavement
subgrade), at moisture content near optimum. Imported sand used as bedding or thermal backfill should be clean, well
graded and free of organic matter. Where pavement is removed, restore with a section at least equal to the existing section.

    cc=d+jooh+hooh+prof+bond+esc; cont=0.05*cc; sioh=0.057*(cc+cont)
    return dict(jooh=jooh,hooh=hooh,profit=prof,bond=bond,escalation=esc,contract=cc,contingency=cont,sioh=sioh,total=cc+cont+sioh)

def bond_premium(B,months=15):
    rem=B; prem=0

        x=min(rem,amt); prem+=x/1000*rate; rem-=x

    prem*=1+0.01*max(0,months-12)
    return prem

# Conveyance Study - 13.8 kV Site Distribution

**Project:** Pacific Crest Space Force Annex (PCSFA), Los Angeles County, California - PCSFA 24-0117

**Solicitation:** FA4610-26-R-0031, Section 01 11 00 Summary of Work: Conveyance Study, Amendment 0002 (2026-08-28)

**Study date:** 2026-09-15  |  **Bid opening:** 2026-10-08  |  **Construction:** 2027-01-04 to 2028-04-03 (15 months), midpoint 2027-08-18

**Route plan:** route_plan.svg (site coordinates in the C-101 frame; solid = CEDB/RMC, dashed = JB/HDD, squares = manholes/pull boxes).

## 1. Executive summary

Seven medium-voltage circuits were studied. The governing criteria (PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3, UFC 3-550-01, UFC 3-520-01, UFGS 33 71 02 and UFGS 26 20 00) permit concrete-encased ductbank (CEDB) for the five site circuits that lie inside the C-101 industrial area and for the underground risers of C06, overhead (OH) for C06 outside the industrial area (IEDS 4.1), and rigid metal conduit (RMC) for the in-building circuit C05. UEDB and DBC are excluded for every site circuit by IEDS 4.2 and HDD as a whole-run method by IEDS 4.3/UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1; OH is not predominant for C01-C04 and C07 because their routes lie inside the industrial area; EMT is excluded by UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.6.7 and both tray types by the 14 in ceiling space at COR-1D/COR-2 and the fully-enclosed requirement for MV cable. Every type was nevertheless priced as RFP 1.4 requires.

Recommended programme total project cost: **$1,856,568** (direct cost $1,312,464).

## 2. Basis of estimate

- Labor: crew-book crews and the PCEC 2026 labor-unit database, with P-405 units converted at 67/80 and the mechanical-puller (0.85) and bucket-truck (0.85) multipliers of the database notes. Loaded rate = base x (1 + burden) + fringe; burden = FICA 7.65% + FUTA 0.60% + CA SUI 3.40% + WC class rate (20.39% line construction, 15.77% inside electrical, 19.00% laborer/operator).
- Equipment: EP 1110-1-8 Region VII (30 Nov 2016) total hourly rates, fuel and FOG adjusted per EP 3.9/3.10 from the Region VII base diesel $2.26/gal to the jobsite $4.38/gal (ratio 1.9381) and gasoline $2.49 to $5.12/gal (ratio 2.0562); rental equipment at RQ-26-0419.
- Materials: quote Q-2608-114 prices x (1 + recommended waste) x PPI adjustment 1.023796 (WPU102603 494.096 / 482.612) on indexed conductor items x 1.095 sales tax.
- Subcontracts: ADD-26-311 (HDD) and PJB-8817 (jack-and-bore) at quoted prices, no waste, tax or adjustment.
- Roll-up: JOOH 9.5%, HOOH 4.5% of direct+JOOH, profit 7.9494% by the weighted guidelines (weights from RFP 3.6 and UFC 3-740-05 11-2.2 for $4.2M, 15 months, 30% subcontracting), bond effective rate 1.2206% from the Sierra Surety Class B schedule with the 3-month (>12 month) surcharge applied to the seven recommended designs, escalation factor 1.019388 from UFS 3-701-01 Table 4-2 interpolated to 2027-08-18 over 2026-09-15, design contingency 5.0% of contract cost and SIOH 5.7% of contract plus contingency. ## 3. Design basis and constraints applied

- Cable: 15 kV, 133%, XLPE, copper-tape shield, aluminum, MV-105; three single conductors per set in one duct. Design current = feeder phase pickup from PDS Rev D. Ampacity from TD-15AL-133 at the governing condition: soil thermal resistivity of the nearest boring raised to the next tabulated value, earth ambient 25 C (factor), next higher circuit count and depth; building raceways 40 C. Short-circuit capability at the 0.5 s backup clearing time checked against the source bus fault current.
- C01/C02: 2 sets of 500 kcmil in 6 in EB-20 ducts, 3 ducts (1 spare), at 30 in cover. C02 rises to 63 in only where it passes beneath the T-2 telecom ductbank (15 in vertical separation); its Mission Drive crossing is a 30 in jack-and-bore. C03: 500 kcmil, 2 ducts (1 spare), 30 in cover except 56 in at the G-4 gas crossing (15.5 in vertical separation). C04: 250 kcmil, 2 ducts (1 spare), 6 in EB-20 at 30 in cover; the DC-1 crossing is a 6 in HDPE SDR 11 bore (D/d 3.90). C06: overhead 1/0 ACSR (196 A at 40 C) on seven wood poles outside the industrial area, with 350 kcmil underground risers (2 x 5 in EB-20 ducts, 1 spare) at SS-1 and at the GH-1 pad; the 350 kcmil riser is retained for its 23.3 kA short-circuit rating (250 kcmil would give 16.6 kA against a 16.5 kA bus, a 0.6% margin). C07: 250 kcmil, 2 ducts (1 spare), 5 in. C05: 2 sets of 250 kcmil in two 5 in RMC (D/d 3.63, fill 22.8%).
- Routes avoid retained-tree protection zones (1 ft radius per inch DBH), maintain 5 ft horizontal / 12 in vertical separation from the SUE-located utilities, do not open-cut Perimeter Road, Mission Drive, the MB-1 access drive or channel DC-1, and cross Mission Drive by jack-and-bore (RGS) and the channel by HDD (HDPE SDR 11, 140 ft, 50 ft beyond each bank).
- Manholes: precast 6x8x7 ft, 8 ft excavation with 2 ft clearance, box shield, 0.5 ft rock base, spaced <=600 ft with the submitted pulling calculation and within 100 ft of pad-mounted transformers; field long-sweep bends 25 ft radius elsewhere. Trench excavations below 5 ft use vertical sides (no shield); the 54 in-cover C03 segment is 5.3 ft deep and is shielded.
- Cable pulling: every pull calculated from 100 lb feed tension, manufacturer friction factors, weight correction for the 3-cable configuration, bend-by-bend exponential tension and SWBP at 25 ft field-bend radius (36 in building elbows), against 0.006 lb/circular mil x two conductors (max 10,000 lb) and the approved 600 lb/ft SWBP.
